specificFindings: Chapter3 ending affirms happiness and meaning benefits before expanding the available paths, not discarding both.
May not stable or comfortable contrasts with exhilarating; dramatic does not mean fictional or constantly contented.
Chapter4 So far explicitly reviews prior discussion; tea with a friend is an example, not a mandatory activity.
Dedication and chosen realm preserve focused meaning, while closer to happiness/meaning is not an every-person guarantee or rejection of exploration.
Hesse characters are fictional literary examples, not author biography or psychological trial participants.1946 Nobel date is not confused with2020 film adaptation.
Smart/popular pronoun refers to Narcissus. Cloistered does not imply he is unhappy, and the scholar/monastery-head roles belong to the character.
Goldmund wandering artist choice includes costs; no instruction for readers to abandon shelter or security is added.
Worth-experiencing question expresses doubt, not a final proof of all choices being wrong; often and as if preserve frequency and subjective judgement.
At novel end Narcissus questions something missing. The cloister group favourable judgement is attributed, not treated as the narrator absolute objective verdict.
Experiential richness can be missing despite happiness and meaning; Goldmund richness is compatible with hard and unpredictable life, not guaranteed pleasure.
Which life would you choose invites reflection on trade-offs, not a mandatory experimentally verified answer.

Not the only author transitions to Kierkegaard. Aesthetic versus virtuous life is a literary-philosophical dilemma; Author A promotes beauty/adventure and spontaneity, not the book narrator own universal prescriptions.
Author A negative marriage judgement is not assigned to Author B, all married respondents, or the narrator spouse.
Questions2,10,14,20 carry exact relevant context for reference, question function and trade-offs. Source wording, ellipses and stable candidate IDs stay unchanged.
